thread.title: Apple Stock Falls For Fifth Straight Day As Wall Street In 'Full Panic Mode'

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Falls For Fifth Straight Day As Wall Street In 'Full Panic Mode'
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) investors are worried ahead of the company's fiscal second-quarter earnings report, due in a week, as the company's stock has fallen for five straight trading sessions.
X Apple shares lost 1.4% Tuesday to close at 162.94 Apple stock fell below the previous low in its seven-week flat base . It also dropped below its 200-day moving average, taking it further from its buy point of 183.60.
Apple has been pressured by reports of weak iPhone sales, especially for its flagship iPhone X handset. A steady drip of reports from Apple's Asian supply chain partners have pointed to lowered production targets for the first half of 2018.
"Heading into Apple's much-anticipated March quarter (report) next week the Street has gone into 'full panic mode,'" GBH Insights analyst Daniel Ives said in a report to clients Tuesday.
 "Supply chain checks out of Asia indicate that June iPhone shipments are trending well below expectations," Ives said. Those reports are likely to neutralize any positive data points, such as higher average selling prices, from the fiscal second-quarter report , he said.
Apple Stock Price Target Cut Ives reiterated his rating of "highly attractive" on Apple stock, but lowered his price target to 200 from 205 to reflect softer-than-expected iPhone demand and lowered estimates for this fiscal year and next.
"While the Street has been anticipating a 'trough June quarter,' the bad news continues to pour in from Asian suppliers and checks with softer demand and $1,000 sticker shock price points on iPhone X translating into another guidance cut expected next week on the horizon," Ives said.
The big question now is what iPhone demand will look like after the June quarter as Apple begins to ramp up production on its 12th-generation iPhones, expected to debut in September, Ives said.
Ives remains positive on Apple largely because of the huge number of iPhone users expected to upgrade to new handsets in the year or so ahead.
"We estimate Apple has roughly 350 million iPhones that are in the window of opportunity to upgrade over the next 12 to 18 months," he said. "Now it's about which model and price point 'strike a chord' for these customers to ultimately upgrade."
